mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that precede higher corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals restrictive monetary policy that compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad-based consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by at least 1% month-over-month, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial production contraction (INDPRO < 100), S&P 500 returns turn negative over 20 days due to recessionary fears amplified by monetary tightening cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of INDPRO < 100 periods during monetary tightening, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflation that elevates real interest rates, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of CPIAUCSL increase periods, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) rises above 4.5%, it signals labor market deterioration that reduces corporate profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of UNRATE > 4.5% instances, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL indicate inflation-driven monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days due to real rate pressure.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increase by ≥0.1% and ≥0.2% month-over-month, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation monetary tightening regimes (CPIAUCSL > 315 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), S&P 500 returns turn negative over 20 days due to dual pressure on real rates and earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of CPIAUCSL > 315 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5% periods, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows.
